excerpt: significance: [p] is (fully) grounded in D only if the connecting questions with respect to [p] and D lack cognitive significance.
overview: The significance principle supplies the first substantive premise of the central argument. It links full grounding to a broadly epistemic condition: once the relevant entities and facts are properly grasped, the question why the grounded fact obtains given the grounds should not remain a live substantive explanatory demand.
title: Significance Principle
